source.title: Watching the AI Watchdogs: A Fairness and Robustness Analysis of AI Safety Moderation Classifiers

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates moderation classifiers, not the fine-tuning, token-position, or refusal behavior of safety-trained chat models in the claim. It cites the original fine-tuning paper but does not test or use its finding.
record.gate_note: The study reports robustness results for closed-source safety moderation classifiers under input perturbations. These are related findings about moderation-label changes, but are not results on harmful-request compliance by chat models or the specific interventions in V1–V7.
record.test_reason: The study audits fairness and robustness of four closed-source moderation classifiers (OpenAI Moderation, Perspective, GCNL, Clarifai) under paraphrase/backtranslation perturbations. It does not fine-tune chat models, measure harmful-request compliance, per-token KL, prefilling, parameter localization, or deepening training. It cites Qi et al. 2023 only as motivation for moderation filtering of fine-tuning data.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Authors conclude the four moderation APIs show fairness gaps (OpenAI least fair, especially on sexual orientation; GCNL near the random baseline) and significant robustness gaps: LLM paraphrases flip many unsafe comments to safe, so the guardrails can be bypassed.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates closed-source moderation APIs under input perturbations; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning method.
record.method_sensitivity: Perturbation method matters: the authors report larger robustness errors for LLM-based perturbations than for backtranslation across the evaluated APIs and datasets. They also report that the choice of classification threshold can improve or worsen fairness.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-3.5-Turbo paraphrases change moderation-classifier labels far more than backtranslation (e.g. OpenAI Moderation 20–32% vs ~5% robustness error, Table 2), and mostly flip initially unsafe comments to safe for OpenAI, Perspective, Clarifai (Figure 4b).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Moderation classifiers used as fine-tuning-data guardrails can be bypassed by semantics-preserving LLM paraphrase; this is about classifier labels, not chat-model refusal depth.

record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (NAACL), 2025
record.problems: The study evaluates proprietary moderation classifiers rather than chat-model harmful-request behavior. The reported robustness errors do not establish harmful completion rates. The authors note that the OpenAI moderation model and GPT-3.5-Turbo perturbation model may be updated; perturbations sometimes alter harmfulness, and the evaluation is limited to English text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4 transition-matrix values and Table 4 qualitative examples are not extracted as additional rows; the tabled robustness-error results are recorded in R1–R40, and the prose summary of unsafe-to-safe changes is included in fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and resulting harmful compliance; not studied.
Benign fine-tuning eroding safety; not studied.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models; not studied.
Prefill, suffix or decoding attacks on chat-model refusal; perturbations target classifiers, not chat models.
Localization of safety in parameters; not studied.

record.verdict_notes: Rows R1–R40 correctly linked to none; values match Table 2. Relation cites_only/T6 confirmed. Manual check found 19/200 Jigsaw and 16/100 Reddit perturbed harmful inputs became harmless, so most flips are label changes, not harm removal. This is relevant context for the fits_no_version finding but not to any version.

versions.untested_parts: Per-token KL divergence across aligned and base chat-model response positions.
Compliant-opening prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes applied to chat models.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Training to deepen safety behavior and its robustness.
